learning_outcomes.title: Multiplication properties of exponents
learning_outcomes.statement: Multiply monomials and simplify expressions using multiplication properties of exponents.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Add exponents in a product; multiply exponents in a power. Apply the power to the coefficient too.

questions.instruction: A square field has side length 5x³y⁵. What is its area in terms of x and y?
questions.stem: A square field has side length 5x³y⁵. What is its area in terms of x and y?

answer.model_answer_and_marking: A=s²=(5x³y⁵)²=25x⁶y¹⁰. Square the coefficient (3), multiply each exponent by 2 (5), final expression (2).

questions.instruction: A cube-shaped shipping box has side length 4m⁸n⁴. What is its volume in terms of m and n?
questions.stem: A cube-shaped shipping box has side length 4m⁸n⁴. What is its volume in terms of m and n?

answer.model_answer_and_marking: V=s³=(4m⁸n⁴)³=64m²⁴n¹². Cube the coefficient (3), multiply each exponent by 3 (5), final expression (2).

parts.prompt: What must be true about p and q for the expressions to be equal? Give an example.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: For positive m≠1, require p+q=pq, or (p−1)(q−1)=1 (3). Example p=q=2 (2). Without that assumption, m=1 makes both expressions equal for all defined p,q; other bases require domain care.

parts.prompt: Assuming m, p and q are positive integers, can (mᵖ)(mᑫ) > (mᵖ)ᑫ ever be true? Explain.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Yes. Take m=2 and p=q=1: 2·2=4>2¹=2 (3). For m>1 compare exponents p+q and pq (2).

questions.instruction: For nonzero real a and b and integers m and t, simplify and explain.
questions.stem: For nonzero real a and b and integers m and t, simplify and explain. (-\frac{a^m}{b^t})^{2t}

parts.prompt: Apply the power rules and explain the sign.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Since 2t is even, (−1)²ᵗ=1 (3). Multiply the numerator exponents to get 2mt (3), and denominator exponents to get 2t² (3); final quotient (1). Nonzero a,b make all integer powers defined.

steps.title: Calculate mode
steps.text: Select Calculate. Use the (−) key for a negative number, and parentheses around fractions and negative bases.

steps.title: Numerical check
steps.text: Substitute {'a': 2, 'b': 3, 'm': 4, 't': 5} into the original expression and each proposed expression. Repeat with different allowed values. Matching values support a check; prove equivalence algebraically.

steps.title: Enter and evaluate
steps.text: Enter the expression below, then =. Use S⇔D when a decimal is required.

parts.prompt: For each equation, write the related expression and record the power of x.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: x=x¹ (power 1), x·x=x² (power 2), x·x·x=x³ (power 3). One mark per row.

parts.prompt: Graph each equation using a graphing calculator.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Correct line, upward parabola and increasing cubic through the origin. One mark per graph.

parts.prompt: Classify each graph as linear or nonlinear.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: y=x is linear; y=x² and y=x³ are nonlinear. One mark for all three correct.

parts.prompt: Explain how to determine whether an equation, or its related expression, is linear or nonlinear without graphing.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: After simplification, y=ax+b is linear (2); higher powers of x such as x² and x³ are nonlinear (1).

steps.title: TABLE mode
steps.text: Select Table. In SETUP → Table, select f(x) only (or leave g(x) blank when prompted). fx‑991EX generates values, not a graph.

steps.title: Enter f(X)
steps.text: Enter X^2. Use ALPHA and the key labelled X, then =.

steps.title: Read and plot
steps.text: Read X and f(X), copy the pairs into the table, then plot them by hand. For a quadratic, include the vertex and two points on each side.
